title: Diversity metric audit: which homogeneity measures actually detect safety-relevant convergence?

original_idea.body:
# Diversity metric audit

On a paraphrase-constructed dataset (surface-similar-but-diverse and surface-different-but-identical), compute several homogeneity metrics and score how well each tracks ground-truth semantic/safety convergence; recommend a robust metric. Embeddings + paraphrase generation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (better metrics improve monitoring) but the catastrophic link is methodological/indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: construct paraphrase-controlled dataset, compute metrics, score against ground truth; dataset construction needs care.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (metric recommendation) but constructing the controlled dataset is a real dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: foundational methodological tooling, no internal access, labs unlikely to prioritize.

novelty.reasoning: Metric validation is a recognized gap; this specific safety-convergence audit may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Metric audits exist generally; the safety-relevant-convergence framing is plausibly open.
